digest.top_line: BEACON-HCC: 20-expert Delphi re-stages HCC by burden + vascular invasion, naming EBRT/SBRT and TARE first-class locoregional options rather than salvage.
digest.tldr: Hepatobiliary carried the day, and the news is allocational, not empirical: a burden-and-Vp-based framework that routes Class 1A-3B to SBRT or TARE alongside resection/ablation, citing RTOG 1112 and DOSISPHERE for the RT/TARE rationale. Concordance 96.6% vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025 is opinion vs opinion, not an outcome.

sites.intro: One consensus document, no efficacy endpoint: what moves is where SBRT sits in the algorithm, not what it delivers.

studies.name: BEACON-HCC
studies.tldr: 20-expert Delphi framework re-allocates HCC treatment by tumor burden and vascular invasion; 96.6% expert concordance vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025.
details: 🔍 Modified Delphi, 20 North American experts across hepatology, med onc, surgery, radiology, rad onc
🔍 Pilot validation: 29 real-world cases scored against external expert consensus

details.text: 📊 BEACON class vs BCLC 2025 / AJCC v8, and what the framework changed

rows: Vp1-2 may be amenable to TARE, SBRT, resection
Macrovascular invasion may be amenable to local therapy
Extensive intrahepatic spread treated as systemic process

details: 📊 Key move for RT: EBRT/SBRT and TARE named as first-class locoregional options, not salvage
🔍 Panel states no high-quality data show superiority of one locoregional therapy over another
🔍 Class 4A (>50% burden or multifocal Vp3/4): TACE, TARE, EBRT not routinely indicated outside palliation
🔗 Class 3B rationale cites NRG/RTOG 1112 (Vp3/4 in 63%), SBRT vs sorafenib OS trend p=0.06
🔗 Class 1D rationale cites DOSISPHERE: personalized dosimetry ORR 71 vs 36%, OS 26.6 vs 10.7 mo

⚠️ Panel agreement was NOT uniform across classes; per-class values are in a table whose row pairing the source text does not resolve, so no class-level agreement figure is quotable here. Range spanned 11/16 to 18/18 initially
⚠️ Concordance is opinion measured against opinion: external experts vs a framework the same community wrote. No survival endpoint
⚠️ n=29 pilot cases, single scoring exercise; empiric validation via HCC-Live Consortium is planned, not done

verdict.rationale: Delphi consensus framework, not a trial. Its 96.6% vs 72.4% figure is expert-agreement, not an outcome. Empiric validation deferred to HCC-Live Consortium.
verdict.audience: HCC across all stages, North American practice

studies.significance: The framework moves EBRT/SBRT and TARE out of the BCLC footnote and into the allocation table itself: Classes 1A, 1B, 1C, 2 and 3A are all flagged as "elevates SBRT and TARE" relative to BCLC 2025. For a rad onc, this is the citation that supports being at the HCC tumor board earlier, at unifocal ≤3 cm rather than only after TACE failure.
studies.monday_clinic: In a Child-Pugh A patient with unifocal HCC 3-8 cm who is not a resection or transplant candidate, this framework supports SBRT or TARE as a named locoregional option rather than a post-TACE fallback; it does not extend to >50% tumor burden (Class 4A), where the panel advises against routine locoregional therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Modified **Delphi** consensus, **20** North American experts spanning hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology and radiation oncology. Iterative discussion plus voting, with repeat voting on classes that failed to converge in round 1.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: No efficacy endpoint. The pilot metric was **concordance** between external expert treatment decisions and framework recommendations across **29** real-world cases, benchmarked against BCLC 2025.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: External expert decisions matched BEACON-HCC in **28 of 29 cases (96.6%)** vs **72.4%** for BCLC 2025. The single discordant case was combination systemic plus locoregional therapy for tumor extending into the right atrium.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **EBRT (including SBRT) and TARE are promoted to named locoregional options** across Classes 1A through 3A, where BCLC 2025 does not list them at the same level. The panel states there are **few high-quality data** showing superiority of any one locoregional therapy, so selection rests on tumor size, location, liver function and local expertise. No dose or fractionation is specified.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Divergence from BCLC 2025 is structural, not evidentiary: BEACON splits by intrahepatic burden, vascular invasion depth (Vp1-2 vs Vp3-4) and adverse prognostic markers rather than by BCLC stage. Class 1D (Vp1-2) sits in BCLC advanced (C) yet is treated as potentially local-therapy amenable.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents North American HCC practice with access to transplant, TARE and SBRT. Does not represent Child-Pugh C or ECOG ≥2 patients, for whom the panel directs symptom-directed care.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Agreement varied by class and the source table's rows cannot be reliably paired to their values, so per-class agreement is not quotable. The concordance exercise tested a framework against experts drawn from the same community, and the 29-case pilot has no outcome data behind it.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Classes 1A, 1B, 1C, 2 and 3A are explicitly flagged as "elevates SBRT and TARE" relative to BCLC 2025, which is the citation supporting RT presence at HCC boards from unifocal ≤3 cm onward. Note the boundary: Class 4A (>50% burden) says EBRT is not routinely indicated outside palliation.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Systemic therapy stays the cornerstone for Class 3B, 4A and 4B, but the framework carves out cases where systemic therapy may beat TACE for large or multifocal burden, and it explicitly does not recommend adjuvant therapy after complete response to surgery or locoregional treatment. ICI plus TACE remains case-by-case, not routine.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Resection is preferred without CSPH and transplant with it, but the framework opens surgical reconsideration after deep durable response to locoregional or systemic therapy, including Vp1-2 disease. It cites an RCT reporting better outcomes with resection after neoadjuvant radiation than up-front resection in Class 3B.

open_questions: Head-to-head SBRT vs TARE vs TACE in liver-localized HCC
TARE with personalized dosimetry vs ICI systemic therapy in Vp1-2 disease
Neoadjuvant radiation before resection in macrovascular invasion

papers.title: BEACON-HCC: Best evidence and north american consensus on treatment allocation for hepatocellular carcinoma
authors: on behalf of HCC-Live Steering Committee
papers.abstract: Background : Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Optimal treatment decisions are challenging, and existing treatment allocation frameworks may not fully reflect the evolving therapeutic landscape or contemporary clinical practices in North America. Methods : Using a modified Delphi process, a multidisciplinary panel of 20 North American experts in hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology developed a consensus-based treatment framework for HCC, termed the BEACON-HCC system. The framework was informed by current evidence and expert opinion through iterative discussion and voting. In a pilot study using 29 real-world patient cases, we assessed concordance between external expert recommendations and BEACON-HCC recommendations and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) 2025 treatment recommendations. Results : The BEACON-HCC treatment allocation framework diverges from prior frameworks by incorporating nuanced clinical features such as degree of intrahepatic tumor burden and vascular invasion, and adverse tumor prognostic markers, to align treatment allocation with tumor biology and therapeutic potential. Key innovations include the incorporation of emerging modalities such as external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), transarterial radioembolization (TARE), and systemic-locoregional combination therapies. In the pilot exercise, expert treatment decisions showed 96.6% concordance with BEACON-HCC recommendations and 72.4% concordance with BCLC recommendations. Conclusions : BEACON-HCC is a consensus-based framework for treatment allocation that incorporates the expanding range of therapeutic options available to patients in the North American HCC population. Expert treatment decisions showed a high concordance with the BEACON-HCC system; further validation using empiric clinical data is planned through the HCC-Live Consortium.
